relationships.subject: SIRT1
relationships.evidence_quote: Mechanistically, SIRT1 deacetylates the p65/RelA subunit of NF‐κB, reducing its transcriptional activity and thereby blunting RANKL‐driven osteoclast differentiation and function [21, 25].

relationships.subject: SIRT1
relationships.evidence_quote: Upregulation of SIRT1 in osteocytes suppresses Sost transcription, lowering sclerostin output and thereby releasing inhibition of WNT/β‐catenin signaling in osteoblasts.

relationships.subject: SIRT1
relationships.evidence_quote: It promotes osteoblast differentiation (via RUNX2, Bmi1, metabolic support) while inhibiting osteoclastogenesis through NF‐κB suppression.

key_findings: Review: SIRT1 promotes osteoblastogenesis and suppresses osteoclastogenesis and marrow adiposity.
Direct evidence linking SIRT1 to bone marrow edema is limited and indirect.
